source.title: Using physics-inspired Singular Learning Theory to understand grokking & other phase transitions in modern neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper uses Anthropic’s Toy Models of Superposition as an experimental setting, but its results concern a free-energy/time-to-transition hypothesis, not whether sparse features are represented as overlapping directions or the geometry of those representations.
record.gate_note: The paper reports that results for TMS transition timing vary with the transition-detection method. These results do not measure feature overlap, feature sparsity or importance, polysemanticity, SAE features, or feature dimensionality, so they do not test any listed claim version. The paper’s modulo-arithmetic results concern grokking and are not about superposition.
record.test_reason: The study trains Toy Models of Superposition only as a testbed for an Arrhenius-style free-energy/transition-time hypothesis. It reports no measurement of feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity dependence, geometry, polysemanticity, SAE features or feature dimensionality. It mentions polygon-shaped weight transitions only as background, not as a measured result. Because it relies on the TMS setup as a tool without testing the claim, T4 fits better than the reader's T6/discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors report mixed evidence for the Arrhenius-style hypothesis. The modular addition runs show a consistent negative slope, though with low R². The TMS result is inconclusive and sensitive to transition detection. The authors also report LLC scaling results for polynomial regressors, low-rank networks and autoencoders.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce or evaluate the original superposition method; it uses TMS to study a different hypothesis about transition timing.
record.method_sensitivity: For TMS, the reported direction of the linear fit depends on the transition-detection method.

fits_no_version.finding: In TMS, the fit of free-energy change against log transition time slopes upward with smoothed transition detection. A non-smoothing detector gives a downward slope, and the authors call the result inconclusive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In TMS training, the relationship between SLT free-energy change and time to phase transition depends on the transition-detection method.

record.problems: The TMS result is explicitly described as inconclusive and highly sensitive to transition detection. The reported result does not assess the listed superposition claims.
record.rows_left_out: The modulo-arithmetic experiment and the LLC scaling experiments concern other questions and do not report results bearing on the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Overlapping, near-orthogonal feature directions; sparsity-dependent transition; regular geometry. The paper names polygon transitions as background but does not measure them.
Capacity competition and dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Feature spreading or SAE recovery in LLMs.
SAE features as complete, stable, canonical units.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T6/discusses label understates the study's reliance on TMS. The study trains 60 TMS models as its experimental setting, which makes it a uses-without-test (T4) case. No verdicts are given because none of the results bear on the superposition versions.

versions.untested_parts: Feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry.
Capacity pressure, polysemanticity, and dedication or sharing of dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity can arise without capacity pressure.
Feature distribution across neurons and recovery of sparse features with a dictionary.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
